A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SimZSS and retain the same central framework and benchmarks. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and ImageNet classification results, backbone and hyperparameter ablations, scalability experiments, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds broader classification evaluation, concept-bank removal experiments, resolution tests, and visual-prototype segmentation analyses.

M1.justification: The main concept-extraction pipeline and objectives in Equations (1)-(10) remain unchanged. However, v3 Appendix A.1 introduces a backbone-specific adaptation: ViT-L/14 training uses average-pooled dense visual features instead of the poorly aligned [CLS] representation.

E1.justification: Classification expands from ImageNet-1k to a suite described as 38 datasets, including medical images, remote sensing, fine-grained recognition, and synthetic spatial/counting tasks (v3 Section 4.4 and Figure 5). The training datasets and eight segmentation settings are retained. Appendix A.3 also introduces evaluation using labeled visual prototypes.

E2.justification: v3 adds CLIP to the segmentation comparisons in Tables 1-2 and adds CLIPSurgery, GEM, SCLIP, and ProxyCLIP in the training-free comparison in Table 7. Table 8 introduces visual-prototype, dense nearest-neighbor, and linear-segmentation comparisons. CLIP-DNOiser and CLIP-DINOiser are the same retained baseline, despite the spelling change.

E3.justification: The stated COCO training budget changes from 10 epochs in v1 Appendix A.1.3 to 4M samples, approximately 6.6 epochs, in v3 Section 4.1.3; this does not establish that retained results were rerun. New settings include 1.6B LAION samples, ViT-L/14, training resolutions of 224 versus 448, evaluation resolutions of 448 versus 896, and visual-prototype/background controls.

E4.justification: Table 4 replaces the experiment excluding Pascal VOC classes from the concept bank with complete removal of concept-bank filtering. v3 also adds larger-backbone and text-encoder controls, visual-versus-textual prototype and background analyses, and training/evaluation resolution sweeps. The earlier hyperparameter, scalability, and runtime analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new average classification accuracy aggregates datasets and does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The principal retained segmentation and ImageNet scores remain numerically unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results. Examples include 69.3% ImageNet accuracy with the new 1.6B-sample training budget, classification-suite averages, and backbone, resolution, and comparator results. Table 4 removes the VOC-exclusion result of 88.1 foreground mIoU and reports 89.2 without any concept bank; these are different settings, not a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The representation definitions and mathematical objectives in Equations (1)-(10) are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3's new bottleneck explanations are empirical interpretations rather than formal derivations.

C1.justification: The three listed contributions and the abstract's claim of state-of-the-art performance on seven of eight benchmarks remain. v3 adds an explicit inference-efficiency claim in the conclusion and more explicitly argues in the introduction that learning suitable visual representations is harder than aligning the text encoder.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations and limitations. Appendix A.3 argues that dataset specificity and heterogeneous backgrounds limit performance beyond the modality gap. Appendices A.1 and A.6 discuss token misalignment and resolution-dependent semantic alignment as explanations for failures. Section 4.5 newly emphasizes that localized consistency, rather than concept-bank filtering, drives most of the benefit.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code/pretrained-model link and a reproducibility statement describing a planned README, explicitly specifies the 448-by-448 inference window, and documents pooling procedures for new experiments. Most existing architecture, optimization, concept-bank, and hardware details are retained or relocated. The PDFs document the resource announcement but do not verify external availability.

R1.justification: v3 expands citations to training-free segmentation, captioning, and visual-feature refinement, and Appendix A.2 discusses SimZSS's model-size, adaptation, and inference-cost advantages against training-free approaches. Its central positioning around frozen visual representations remains. Publication updates to retained works, including CRIBO and CLIP-DINOiser, do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: v3 selectively rewrites the introduction and concept-bank discussion, moves experimental setup from Appendix A to Section 4.1, and moves scalability from Section 4.4 to Appendix A.5. It also adds a reproducibility statement and edits author/header text. Most method exposition and the overall main-section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1-2 are reorganized by training source, Table 3 gains training-budget and average-accuracy columns, and new comparison and diagnostic tables substantially expand the displays. Figure 5 adds a large classification bar chart. Figures 1-3 retain their visual content, while the existing scalability Figure 4 moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical scrutiny through concept-bank removal, failure-condition analyses, broader classification evaluation, and relevant training-free comparisons. These gains make the method's strengths and limits easier to assess. However, the explicit VOC class-exclusion control is lost, and the retained seven-of-eight state-of-the-art claim is not reconciled with stronger competitors reported in Appendix Table 7. The net quality gain is positive but qualified.
